taxonomy.confirmed-bug: The implementation does not meet its own documented claim. Fix the framework, keep the test.
taxonomy.policy-decision: The secure expectation is defensible but product policy may intentionally allow it. Ratify or change policy, then keep/adjust/remove the test.
taxonomy.false-positive: The assertion is too strict or the behaviour is legitimate. Rewrite or remove the test.
taxonomy.guard: Passing test that pins a property which is currently safe.

reproStatus.note: All audit assertions pass; the suite is a regression gate.

rootCauses.title: Trust-domain collapse
rootCauses.description: Gate policy, validator code and CI enforcement live in the same repository as the AI agent they constrain. Nothing is pinned, signed, or immutable at enforcement time.

rootCauses.title: Fail-open defaults
rootCauses.description: Missing mode, skipped gates and unresolved globs resolve to success instead of failure.

rootCauses.title: Attestation not bound to identity or content
rootCauses.description: Sign-off checks working-tree bytes against an older commit, trusts a self-asserted author email, and never binds approval to artifact hashes.

rootCauses.title: Structural-only validation
rootCauses.description: PRD, architecture and test gates validate headings and token counts, not substance or execution.

rootCauses.title: Rule-engine QA gap
rootCauses.description: Security rules are regexes without positive-fixture liveness tests, so dead rules (SEC-004, multi-line SEC-014) ship undetected.

rootCauses.title: CI supply-chain hygiene
rootCauses.description: Mutable action tags, install scripts, persisted credentials, write tokens around untrusted code, masked failures and no dependency review.

rootCauses.title: Tool-surface confinement
rootCauses.description: MCP tools accept traversal paths, scan outside the workspace, and return production-ready verdicts from self-test fixtures.

tests.recommendedAction: Reject gates.disable for required gates. If a break-glass path is needed, require an explicit, recorded, time-boxed override.
Remove gates.validators from adopter config; validators are framework-owned and fixed per gate id.

Keep --allow-missing for local bootstrap but (a) never print a production-ready claim, (b) make skip counts a non-zero exit in CI, (c) require a recorded opt-out. Ratify whether the flag may exist at all in project mode.
tests.statusNote: Fail-closed implementation; the product decision about whether --allow-missing should exist remains.

tests.recommendedAction: Require an explicit mode. Missing or invalid mode must throw, matching skillforge.config.schema.json.
Decide whether monorepo/sibling-package targets are supported. If yes, add a configured allowedRoots list and reject everything else; if no, reject all paths outside the repo.
Fail when any configured non-optional glob resolves to zero files (or emit an explicit UNRESOLVED status that blocks CI).
Validate skillforge.config.json against its schema at load time; reject unknown keys and unsupported override values.
Verify the committed blob (git show HEAD:path) or hash the working-tree content and require it to equal the committed blob before running identity checks.
Require a mandatory artifact list with path + SHA-256; verify each hash at gate time. Rename the field from 'Commit / Artifact Hash' to 'Commit' and add a real artifact binding.
Compare the signing key fingerprint/UID (%GF/%GS) to allow-listed reviewer keys. Do not use the author email as the identity.
Use the signed approval date (or author date) for TTL and reject documents whose approval date is in the future or older than the TTL.
A denylist is not a security control. Prefer the allow-list of reviewer key fingerprints (AUD-S03) and treat this test as documentation of the heuristic's limits. Rewrite or retire after S03.
Parse the sign-off with the fence-aware markdown parser and read fields only from the document header block.
Agree the machine-readable verdict contract. Recommendation: always return {mode, demo, artifactHashes, signerFingerprint} and never authorize deployment when demo=true.
Fix the SEC-004 regex (remove the empty-matching \s* alternative) and add a positive fixture to the normal test suite.
Scan .env/YAML/Dockerfile regardless of comment marker; only skip comments for code extensions, and add inline suppression syntax.
Scan multi-line windows or the parsed config for SEC-014 so formatting does not evade detection.
Decide scanning policy for build outputs. If dist/build are intentionally excluded, document it as an explicit trust assumption and add an opt-in --include-build-output flag; otherwise scan them.
tests.statusNote: Build outputs are out of scope by default; --include-build-output opts in.

tests.recommendedAction: Add a rule-liveness test requiring at least one positive fixture per SEC-* rule; this is the durable fix that prevents RC-5 regressions.
Define a per-severity blocking policy in framework-owned config. Recommended default: HIGH and CRITICAL block; MEDIUM blocks in CI; LOW warns.
Include untracked files in diff mode (git status --porcelain) or document that --staged is mandatory for pre-commit.
Execute the project test command in the Phase 5 gate and use the real exit code; keep static counts as an additional heuristic.
Require a minimum number of executed tests (from the runner report) rather than declared tests.
Ratify the traceability rule. Recommendation: require citations for tests mapped to FR-/EC- IDs and fail the gate only for tests that claim a requirement mapping.
Define the minimum PRD content contract (non-empty FR bodies, AC per FR, NFR targets). The current 'structural only' contract is coherent but undersells the README claim.
Count only non-empty Mermaid bodies and validate the diagram parses.
Decide whether ADR existence is required at Phase 3 or only before release. If required, fail; if progressive, keep the warning and document it.
tests.statusNote: ADR absence is a Phase 3 warning by ratified policy.

tests.recommendedAction: Validate skillName against ^[a-z0-9-]+$ and assert the resolved path stays under .agents/skills.
Confine audit_security paths to the workspace root by default; add an explicit, documented opt-in for external paths.
Return a structured verdict with mode; never emit a production-ready claim when mode is self-test.
Pin all actions to 40-character commit SHAs and manage updates via Dependabot.
Use npm ci --ignore-scripts in CI; add a separate, reviewed step for packages that genuinely need install scripts.
Set persist-credentials: false on checkouts that precede untrusted execution.
Remove || true from gate/diff/scorecard steps and handle missing reports explicitly.
Run gates from an immutable pinned source and add a protected-path guard plus CODEOWNERS. Verify server-side branch protection as part of acceptance.
Split evaluation (read-only, no untrusted code) from commenting (write, no code execution).
Declare permissions: {} at workflow level and grant the minimum per job.
Operational policy, not a code bug. Recommended: add Dependabot for npm and github-actions with a review SLA.
Operational policy. Recommended: add actions/dependency-review-action or npm audit --audit-level=high as a required check.
Keep. Add to the normal test suite as a regression guard.

ratificationChecklist: AUD-G03: may --allow-missing exist in project mode? If yes, what must it print/exit in CI?
AUD-G05: are artifact paths outside the repository a supported monorepo scenario? If yes, define allowedRoots.
AUD-S05: confirm the denylist is documentation-only and superseded by key-fingerprint allow-listing.
AUD-S07: confirm the machine-readable attestation verdict contract.
AUD-R04: are dist/build/bin in scope for the security audit? If not, record the trust assumption.
AUD-R06: confirm the per-severity blocking policy (recommended: HIGH/CRITICAL always, MEDIUM in CI).
AUD-T03: confirm whether FR-/EC- citations are mandatory for all tests.
AUD-D01: confirm the minimum PRD content contract.
AUD-D03: is an ADR required at Phase 3 or only before release?
AUD-C08/C09: confirm dependency-update and vulnerability-review policy.
